title: Is this worth continuing to develop.
author: Enarian__Lead_Dev
selftext:
https://youtu.be/eSFP6Fl6hpk?si=GjvAnW7IGqofeJfu

Prototype space station defence game in a Homeworld style with block built ships and stations etc.

Taken a week in my spare time to get this far..

comments.author: MindCrusader
comments.body:
1. The graphics are really laggy
2. The gameplay loop doesn't look interesting 

The 1st problem can always be fixed, but for the second one you need to have an idea that is interesting. Try to answer yourself, without lying, if you would spend 100 hours playing your game without getting bored. What do you miss. Is there enough challenge. What player can do differently without forcing him to play your way. And possibly a lot more questions

Keep trying and focus on the mechanics first, you do not have to focus on UX or graphics just yet. Once you have a fun gameplay loop, you build around it

replies.author: Enarian__Lead_Dev
replies.body: Ive enjoyed playing it while testing but yes, its only in its most basic form at the moment whilst i work out whats feasible. I can provide you with access if you wanted to give it a go..

replies.author: MindCrusader
replies.body: Sorry, no time for that, I don't even have time to prototype my own idea :)

replies.author: MinimusMaximizer
replies.body: As someone using SDL with Claude, it does really stupid framerate killing things by default like reading the backbuffer which requires syncing the entire GPU each time instead of rendering into a Pixel Buffer Object or for blending effects using a Frame Buffer based on the previous frame. I went from a craptastic \~20 fps to a solid 60+ fps just telling it to find its rendering bottlenecks and get rid of them.

replies.author: Enarian__Lead_Dev
replies.body: Thanks I will check it out

replies.author: Enarian__Lead_Dev
replies.body: Yes its only a prototype so no optomosation yet and it was captured running on my phone so I think all in all it runs pretty well...

comments.author: Ferreteria
comments.body:
Homeworld is still a great game. A week is good rate of progress to get that far. I'm not sure what your AIs capabilities are to really bring this home - I've only used it for a short time myself. What I'm finding is that it's great at prototyping an idea, but not so great at fleshing out your ideas or creating a finished product. 

What tools are you using?

replies.author: Enarian__Lead_Dev
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback. Cursor mainly. All models are built in game by the engine so no meshy etc.

This is my second ai assisted game the other one is approaching steam launch so I have some experience with fleshing it out but not much.

comments.author: Ok-Antelope7968
comments.body: It definitely worth it you could be setting on a good idea here, you can need to focus on mechanics and content. And the thing about making games of this scale is lack of direction or  game replayability so yes focus on content and mechanics

replies.author: Enarian__Lead_Dev
replies.body: Thanks, yes I decided to reduce the scale slightly and focus on the core loop for now.
